parsed.headline: Credit Assessment for Reyes Auto Repair - 250,000 PHP Loan Application

sections.heading: Business overview
paragraphs: Reyes Auto Repair is an automotive repair and maintenance workshop operated by Ramon Reyes in the Philippines.

The business provides mechanical services including change oil, brake pad replacements, aircon servicing, suspension repairs, and engine overhauls as documented in daily transaction logs and premises signage.
The applicant is seeking a loan facility of PHP 250,000 to support ongoing operations and working capital.

sections.heading: Cash flow
paragraphs: The submitted bank statement covers January, February, May, and June 2026, showing an opening balance of PHP 46,786.21 on January 1, 2026, and an ending balance of PHP 56,954.31 on June 30, 2026.

Operating cash inflows consist of regular branch cash deposits (typically ranging between PHP 4,250 and PHP 20,950 per batch) alongside digital payments received via GCash and InstaPay from individual clients.

Cash outflows consist of recurring auto parts purchases from Banawe suppliers, lubricants, utility bills (Meralco, Maynilad, Smartlink), personal withdrawals, and regular GCash transfers to Juan Dela Cruz (PHP 3,000 multiple times monthly).

sections.heading: Revenue quality
paragraphs: According to the 6-month handwritten summary ledger (Buod Enero-Hunyo 2026), total reported revenue was PHP 379,300 across the first half of 2026, averaging approximately PHP 63,217 per month.
However, monthly revenue displays a steady downward trend: PHP 78,400 in January, PHP 68,600 in February, PHP 69,000 in March, PHP 61,950 in April, PHP 55,150 in May, and PHP 46,200 in June 2026.
Customer concentration risk is low, as revenue is generated from numerous small to medium retail service tickets.

sections.heading: Obligations
paragraphs: The bank statements reveal an existing fixed debt obligation in the form of an ongoing BDO auto loan payment of PHP 14,800 debited around the 10th of every month (observed in Jan, Feb, May, and Jun 2026).

This monthly debt service of PHP 14,800 represents over 30% of recent monthly gross revenues (PHP 46,200 in June), significantly constraining free cash flow capacity to take on an additional PHP 250,000 loan.

sections.heading: Document quality
paragraphs: A critical documentation gap exists: the bank statement D01 skips March and April 2026 entirely, jumping directly from February 28 to May 1, 2026, despite claiming to cover 01/01/2026 to 06/30/2026.
Furthermore, document D07 is an exact duplicate ledger of March 2026 (D04) despite being mislabeled as 'Abril 2026', while D05 contains the actual distinct April ledger.
The discrepancies between recorded ledger figures and bank deposits require complete and continuous bank records for proper reconciliation.

sections.heading: Recommendation
paragraphs: The application is placed on hold / request more documents.

The lender must require complete, unbroken bank statements for March and April 2026 and clarification on the declining monthly revenues before assessing repayment capability for the requested PHP 250,000.

concerns.title: Missing Bank Statement Months (March & April 2026)
concerns.claim: The bank statement D01 has 4 pages covering January, February, May, and June 2026, omitting March and April 2026 completely.

concerns.title: Declining Revenue Trend
concerns.claim: Gross revenue reported in the ledger decreased continuously from PHP 78,400 in January 2026 to PHP 46,200 in June 2026, representing a 41% drop.

concerns.title: High Existing Debt Service Ratio
concerns.claim: Monthly BDO auto loan amortization of PHP 14,800 consumes a substantial portion of net monthly earnings (net income of PHP 36,950 in June 2026).

concerns.title: Duplicate / Conflicting Ledger Page
concerns.claim: Document D07 is an identical copy of the March ledger entries (D04) despite bearing the heading 'Abril 2026'.
